purpose: Since the fund layer is a null, test whether the pre-positioning signal appears at the land-ownership + gubernatorial-nomination-discretion layer, using public oversight and reporting only.
scope_and_guardrail: Public reporting and official oversight only. Public officials named in role (governor). Private beneficiaries are referenced only as they appear in the cited public investigations; no dossier compiled. Every row is candidate_only and gated: designating already-owned land is LAWFUL; these rows document a sequence and the official oversight response, and assert no wrongdoing — that adjudication belongs to the named oversight bodies.

documented_instances.statement: ProPublica reported that a West Palm Beach, FL census tract containing the already-owned, operating Rybovich superyacht marina was added to Florida's Opportunity Zone nominations after the owner lobbied then-Gov. Rick Scott; the state had not originally intended to select that tract based on its own poverty/unemployment analysis. Owner's appeal letter April 2018; Scott announced selections ~one week later (April 19, 2018).
documented_instances.mechanism: patient-ownership (land owned before designation) + gubernatorial nomination discretion

documented_instances.statement: ProPublica documented a broader pattern: developers around the country successfully lobbied to add favored tracts (some with already-planned developments) to the program, and governors in some cases granted the designation to politically connected parties.

The designation process drew official oversight: the Treasury Inspector General opened a probe into possible Opportunity Zone abuses, and the Senate Finance Committee chair opened an inquiry into whether the break benefited the politically connected.

forbidden_inference_gate.held: Designating an already-owned parcel is lawful and is precisely the structural pattern the place-formation signature detects; it is not, by itself, evidence of illegality. These rows document a reported sequence and the official oversight response. No candidate is promoted to a finding. Whether any instance constitutes abuse is for the Treasury IG and Senate Finance Committee to determine, not this pipeline.
